title: JPMorganChase's new community outlook survey reveals how Dallas residents view the local economy, housing, careers and their personal finances

# JPMorganChase's new community outlook survey reveals how Dallas residents view the local economy, housing, careers and their personal finances


While Dallas residents remain hopeful about their own financial outlook, roughly one in three are feeling some level of financial strain.


Dallas, TX


---


November 23, 2026


JPMorganChase today released local findings from its first-ever Community Outlook survey of the Greater Dallas/Fort Worth area, measuring how residents view their financial lives, their communities and their aspirations.


Residents believe they can build a solid financial future in Dallas, but they remain clear-eyed about economic pressures and are approaching spending with caution.


According to the findings, 61% of residents say they can achieve their financial goals while staying in their current city. At the same time, 45% describe the local economy as somewhat or very downbeat, and 36% say it is declining compared with a few years ago.


Dallas residents are also watching their budgets. More than half (57%) have cut back on dining out in the past three months, while 41% report spending more on groceries over the past year. Looking ahead to the holidays, 53% plan to spend less on travel than they did last year.


Even with that caution, residents take a more positive view of their own finances: 44% feel very or somewhat positive, while 34% feel somewhat or very strained.


"Dallas residents remain confident in the opportunities available here, even as they make thoughtful choices about how they spend and plan," said Omar Monsivais, Chase’s Oak Cliff Community Manager. "When every dollar has to work harder, our role is to meet people where they are with practical tools and guidance that can help them make informed tradeoffs, build confidence in their financial decisions and continue working toward the goals that matter most to them."


## Housing affordability and the American Dream


Dallas residents shared their top financial goals, their outlook on homeownership and how broader economic conditions are shaping their personal finances. The survey also captured how residents are weighing buying versus renting and what the American Dream means to them.


Dallas residents want to build resilience and plan for the future:


For 44% of survey respondents, peace of mind and financial security is one of their three biggest financial goals right now, making it the most-cited priority. Retirement and long-term savings and building an emergency fund follow, each cited by 27%.


Homeownership remains central to the American Dream:


When defining the American Dream, 52% of Dallas residents point to owning a home, tied with financial independence and followed closely by being able to afford day-to-day expenses without stress at 51%.


Residents are weighing buying and renting:


While 62% agree that owning a home is important for financial stability (34% strongly and 28% somewhat agree), 48% agree strongly or somewhat that renting makes more financial sense for some people.


Many residents avoided major financial problems in the past year:


40% report experiencing none of the financial problems included in the survey, while 30% say they were targeted by a scam call, yet 29% reported that their bank helped them recognize the scam before they sent money or provided any personal information.


## Views of the local job market and entrepreneurship


The survey also explored how Dallas residents view local job opportunities and whether they plan to start businesses of their own.


Residents see a moderate level of job opportunity:


More than half (53%) describe the local job market as having a moderate amount of opportunity, while 29% say it is hard to get a job in Dallas.


Some residents are looking to entrepreneurship:


21% say they plan to start a business within the next two years. Among those who own or plan to start a business, personal passion is the most common motivation at 32%, followed by a lower cost of living or operating at 15% and achieving the American Dream at 12%.


As part of its[American Dream Initiative](https://www.jpmorganchase.com/newsroom/press-releases/2026/american-dream-initiative-announcement) , JPMorganChase is expanding its community banking efforts to help more people build the knowledge and confidence to manage their money, increasing financial health education programming with the goal of reaching 5 million people. The multi-year effort to expand economic opportunity also focuses on advancing small business growth, increasing affordable housing, improving financial health, helping people secure good jobs, expanding access to quality healthcare and strengthening local institutions in Dallas and communities across the country.


For more than 150 years, JPMorganChase has been working to advance an economy that works for all in Greater Dallas, by leveraging its expertise, insights, and resources to help residents, businesses, and communities achieve their goals. Across Greater Dallas the firm serves nearly 3 million consumer customers, nearly 300,000 small business customers and has nearly 17,000 employees.


Since 2021, the firm has provided more than $45 million in philanthropic contributions to support communities in North Texas, including efforts that have helped place more than 400 individuals in full-time employment and nearly 2,000 individuals in internship, apprenticeship or other work-based learning experiences. Between 2021 and 2025, JPMorganChase also financed the construction and preservation of 3,940 affordable housing units in the region.


To learn more about the firm’s impact in Texas, visit[https://www.jpmorganchase.com/communities/dallas](https://www.jpmorganchase.com/communities/dallas)


## About the survey & methodology


The Community Outlook survey was conducted by Morning Consult on behalf of JPMorganChase, measuring how residents view their financial lives, their communities, and their aspirations. Interviews were conducted online between August 24 and September 11, 2026, among a total of 7,800 U.S. adults ages 18 and older, split evenly across 13 metropolitan areas: Boston, Washington, D.C., Miami, Philadelphia, Columbus, Atlanta, Chicago, Dallas/Fort Worth, Seattle, the San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, and Birmingham. Results carry a margin of error of approximately ±4.0 percentage points at the 95% confidence level, and wider for subgroups. Figures for Dallas reflect responses from approximately 602 residents in the Dallas/Fort Worth metropolitan area, including Dallas-Fort Worth-Arlington, TX.
